Under this examination, the available data in some categories are sparse. While some patterns may speak to overall trends in heavy-duty vehicle driving—such as no school bus data on weekends or a lack of transit buses on rural roads—we will not make recommendations for MOVES3 inputs based on categories of low coverage. Figures 1–6 display FleetDNA data density for each available MOVES source type: the four MOVES on-network road types and the two MOVES day types (weekday and weekend). These plots are used to determine which categories will be shown in analysis graphs in later sections of the report. Typically, fewer than five vehicles recorded with less than an hour of data for any hour ID are likely to be considered too low coverage. Usually, close to 30 hours recorded and 30 vehicles driving during some hours of the day constitute a robust sample size. Figure 1 shows data for the source type combination-unit long-haul, of which all categories have strong coverage in number of vehicles and driving time recorded, albeit with fewer vehicles observed driving close to midnight on rural other roads and on weekends. 9 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 1. FleetDNA data density for combination-unit long-haul vehicles Figure 2 shows the data density for the source type combination-unit short-haul vehicles. Urban roads display a high number of recorded hours and vehicles driving from the FleetDNA database; however, urban freeways have slightly less robust data on the weekend and thus have been shaded yellow to indicate their lower sample size. While rural weekdays may have enough data to glean insights (shaded yellow), rural weekends are lacking robust hours with only a handful of vehicles recorded in their category and will not be included in further analyses of speed and distance (shaded gray). Their data will still be recorded in the output .csv files. 10 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 2. FleetDNA data density for combination-unit short-haul vehicles Figure 3 displays the data density for the single-unit short-haul source type, with nearly solid coverage on urban weekdays and weekends, with slightly low coverage on urban freeways on the weekend (shaded yellow). On weekends, rural roads contain data from only a single vehicle driving for small fractions of an hour and will be excluded from further visuals and discussion but included in output data files. On weekdays, the single-unit short-haul vehicles are also rarely recorded on rural roads and will be excluded as well, but again, available in output .csv files for those who are interested.
